headline: On November 4, 1973: The Netherlands goes car-free
captionCards: Highways used only by cyclists and roller skaters
Inspired modern focus on sustainable transportation
instagramCaption:
The Netherlands experiences its first car-free Sunday.
On November 4, 1973, the Netherlands faced a unique day without cars due to the 1973 oil crisis. Highways were filled with cyclists and roller skaters instead of vehicles. This event was a direct result of the Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC) embargo against countries that supported Israel during the Yom Kippur War. The car-free day highlighted the vulnerability of oil-dependent economies. 
Why does this still matter today? It sparked lasting interest in sustainable transportation.
